When the chair speaks

What path did the chair signal? How had the Treasury curve already moved? Open a speech to compare the policy reading with prices recorded before and after it.

In June 2004, Alan Greenspan described a measured withdrawal of accommodation and observed that futures already anticipated tightening. In August 2023, Jerome Powell left another hike open. The September meeting’s implied move rose just 0.5 basis points in the 20-minute window around the start of his remarks. The speech’s direction and its surprise answer different questions.

What moved around the speeches?

Median signed changes in basis points. Each group contains speeches with an assigned direction, a dated Treasury fixing on either side, and an eligible market window. The pre-speech change runs from the fifth to the last fixing before the event.

Selected speeches and their median Treasury changes
Policy readingMatched2Y moved with toneBefore · 2YBefore · 2s10sAcross · 2YAcross · 2s10s

2s10s is the ten-year yield minus the two-year yield. A positive change means the curve steepened. Daily yields reflect multiple expected rates, term premia and other news. Thirty speeches from 2023 onward also carry an options-implied mean for a specified quarter of SOFR and its change before the speech. Five Jackson Hole entries document specific meeting pricing. Each source names its horizon.

How to read the evidence

Policy path. +2 and −2 indicate an explicit baseline of tightening or sustained restraint, or easing or sustained accommodation. +1 and −1 indicate a conditional preference. Zero requires an explicit preference to wait or keep the prevailing stance. A speech with no assigned score stays outside the directional sample. The prior comparison is the previous scored speech by the same chair. The elapsed days show how much time it spans.

Scope. The catalogue covers 122 Greenspan, 169 Bernanke, 43 Yellen, 78 Powell and two Warsh speeches through November 20, 2026. The reviewed subset was selected for identifiable current policy guidance. It supports comparisons of those passages. It cannot estimate how often each chair expressed a view across all appearances. Hearings, press conferences, interviews and Q&A are outside this catalogue. Where a subject can be identified from the title, unscored technical and ceremonial events are labeled separately.

Two chairs with few scored speeches. We screened the full text of all 122 Greenspan and both Warsh entries for current or forward policy guidance. This yielded three readings for Greenspan and none for Warsh. In January 2002 Greenspan described economic risks and past cuts without specifying his next move. In August 2026 Warsh distinguished his vote at the prior meeting from his assessment of new data.

Greenspan’s three policy readingsJanuary 2002 market responseWarsh’s source texts

Market timing. US Treasury par yields are observed near 3:30 p.m. Eastern. Releases after that fixing use the next available fixing. Where a dated historical release cover supplies its time, the speech card links to the cover in FRASER. Unknown times on trading days, releases at the fixing, multiple speeches sharing one interval, and intervals containing an FOMC decision are excluded from the median table. Their available daily data remain visible in the archive. The one-day filter removes intervals spanning more than one calendar day.

Business cycle. Expansion and recession follow the retrospective NBER monthly chronology in the site’s US macro panel. The latest incomplete month is pending. This classification uses information that may have arrived after the speech.
